facets.label: Model class
facets.definition: The model's class as derived from its model type by `api/classes.py`: what it consumes, what it emits and what decision it makes. One value per model. Class is derived, not authored, and says nothing about quality.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Input modalities
facets.definition: Every modality the model accepts as input natively, without a separate model transcribing or captioning it first. `document` means files such as PDF read as documents, not text extracted by the caller.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Output modalities
facets.definition: Every modality the model emits natively. `embedding` is a vector, `score` a relevance or reward number, `label` a class from a fixed or caller-defined set, and `action` a tool or environment action.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Context window
facets.definition: The maximum number of tokens the model accepts in one request, input and output together, as documented by its lab for its largest supported configuration. A provider that serves a smaller window records that on the offering, not here.
facets.subject: model
facets.unit_definition: Tokens as counted by the model's own tokenizer, as documented by its lab. Not words, characters or another model's tokens.

facets.label: Maximum output tokens
facets.definition: The maximum number of tokens the model can emit in one response, including any reasoning tokens the lab counts against the limit, as documented by its lab.
facets.subject: model
facets.unit_definition: Tokens as counted by the model's own tokenizer, as documented by its lab. Not words, characters or another model's tokens.

facets.label: Open weights
facets.definition: `open_weights` when the lab publishes the trained weights for download under any licence, including a gated or restrictive one; `closed_weights` otherwise. Says nothing about the licence terms, which are the `licence.*` facets.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Total parameters
facets.definition: The total number of parameters in the released model, counting every expert of a mixture-of-experts model. `not_disclosed` is a state of the fact, never an estimate.
facets.subject: model
facets.unit_definition: A count of trainable weights (not billions; 7e9 is written 7000000000).

facets.label: Active parameters
facets.definition: The number of parameters used to process one token. Equal to the total for a dense model; for a mixture-of-experts model, as the lab documents it.
facets.subject: model
facets.unit_definition: A count of trainable weights (not billions; 7e9 is written 7000000000).

facets.label: Architecture
facets.definition: The model's architecture family as `ArchitectureType` in `schema/enums.py` names it. An undisclosed architecture is unknown, never inapplicable.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Routed experts
facets.definition: The number of routed experts in each mixture-of-experts layer, excluding shared experts such as `n_shared_experts`. A single value is recorded only when the config states a uniform count across expert layers.
facets.subject: model
facets.unit_definition: A count of routed experts in one mixture-of-experts layer, excluding shared experts that are used for every token.

facets.label: Experts per token
facets.definition: The number of routed experts selected for one token in each mixture-of-experts layer, excluding always-active shared experts. A single value is recorded only when the config states a uniform count.
facets.subject: model
facets.unit_definition: A count of routed experts in one mixture-of-experts layer, excluding shared experts that are used for every token.

facets.label: Commercial use
facets.definition: Whether the licence governing the model lets a customer use the model or its outputs in a commercial product. `permitted_with_conditions` covers any condition, for example a display or naming duty, a user cap or a field-of-use limit. Attribution means a display or naming duty; keeping a copyright, licence or NOTICE notice, as MIT and Apache-2.0 require, is not a condition. The other `licence.*` facets say which condition applies. A fine-tune carries its base model's terms where the base licence requires derivatives to be distributed under, or remain subject to, those terms.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Licence user cap
facets.definition: The largest number of monthly active users a licensee may serve before the licence requires a separate agreement. `unbounded` when the licence sets no such cap. A fine-tune carries its base model's terms where the base licence requires derivatives to be distributed under, or remain subject to, those terms.
facets.subject: model
facets.unit_definition: Distinct end users in a calendar month, as the licence itself defines the count.

facets.label: Training on outputs
facets.definition: Whether the licence or terms let a customer use the model's outputs to train or improve another model. `restricted` or `prohibited` only where the licence or terms expressly address training on those outputs, on synthetic data from them, or distillation from them. `restricted` when the text expressly allows or forbids it only for some purposes or models, for example not for a competing model, or makes a model trained on outputs a derivative subject to the licence's restrictions. `prohibited` when the text expressly forbids it for every purpose. A generic modification or derivative-works clause that never mentions outputs is not that. Silence is not disclosed. A fine-tune carries its base model's terms where the base licence requires derivatives to be distributed under, or remain subject to, those terms.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Fine-tuning rights
facets.definition: Whether the licence lets a customer modify the model's weights by further training and use the result. Whether a provider offers fine-tuning as a service is `offering.fine_tuning`, a different fact. A fine-tune carries its base model's terms where the base licence requires derivatives to be distributed under, or remain subject to, those terms.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Lab jurisdiction
facets.definition: The country or countries where the lab that trained this model is incorporated, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. Where the lab has a parent company, the parent's country is included too. Says nothing about where the model was based on or where it runs.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Base model lineage
facets.definition: The countries of incorporation of the labs that trained every model this model's weights were derived from (fine-tuned, distilled into, merged or continued from), as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. The empty set when the model was trained from random initialisation. Excludes this model's own lab unless it also trained an ancestor.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Weights hosted in
facets.definition: The countries in which the lab itself stores and serves the weights for the hosted inference it sells first-party, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. The empty set when the lab sells no hosted inference of this model. Where a third-party provider runs the model is `offering.region`, not this.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Base models
facets.definition: The `lab/model-id` of every model this model's weights were directly derived from. The empty set when trained from random initialisation. Backs `origin.base_lineage` with the models themselves.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Release date
facets.definition: The date the lab first made the model generally available to the public, by API or download. A preview or waitlist release counts only if anyone could sign up.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Lifecycle
facets.definition: `deprecated` when the lab has announced a retirement date; `retired` when the lab no longer serves or supports the model; `active` otherwise. Retired models are excluded from decisions unless a spec asks for them.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Knowledge cutoff
facets.definition: The latest date of training data the lab documents for the model. A month is recorded as its first day, and the fact's qualifiers say so.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Deprecation date
facets.definition: The date the lab has announced the model will stop being served by its own API. Unknown until announced; not the date of the announcement.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Tool calling
facets.definition: True when the lab documents that the model emits structured function or tool calls against caller-supplied tool definitions through at least one first-party interface.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Structured output
facets.definition: True when the lab documents constrained output that conforms to a caller-supplied JSON schema. A prompt-only "JSON mode" without a schema guarantee is false.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Effort controls
facets.definition: True when the lab documents a request parameter that changes how much reasoning the model does (a reasoning effort level or thinking budget).
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Batch interface
facets.definition: True when the lab's first-party API offers an asynchronous batch interface for this model. Batch pricing is `offering.price.batch_*`.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Streaming
facets.definition: True when the lab's first-party API can return the response incrementally as it is generated.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Languages
facets.definition: The natural languages the lab documents the model as supporting, as BCP 47 tags. Absence from the set means undocumented, not unsupported.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Fits hardware
facets.definition: The hardware SKUs in `hardware/` on which some published quantisation of the model's weights is estimated to load and run. An estimate, always labelled as one.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Hardware fit indeterminate
facets.definition: The hardware SKUs in `hardware/` for which ModelSpec's single-memory-pool weight-fit formula does not apply. Membership conditions on `model.fits_hardware` treat these device legs as unknown, not as false.
facets.subject: model

facets.label: Provider
facets.definition: The provider in `registry/providers.yaml` that sells the offering and bills the customer for it.
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: Inference region
facets.definition: The countries in which the provider documents that inference for this offering runs, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. A global or routed offering lists every country it may run in. The provider's own region name is a qualifier on the fact.
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: Account tier
facets.definition: The account tier the offering is sold under. A tier is its own offering only when a guaranteed fact differs from the standard tier: price, data handling or an attestation (design §4.1).
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: Input price
facets.definition: The list price of uncached input tokens for a synchronous request. Where the price varies with prompt length, the lowest band, with the band as a qualifier.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: United States dollars per 1,000,000 tokens, at the provider's list price for the offering, before discounts, credits or committed-use pricing. Tokens are counted by the provider's own tokenizer for that model.

facets.label: Output price
facets.definition: The list price of output tokens, including reasoning tokens the provider bills as output, for a synchronous request, lowest band as for input.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: United States dollars per 1,000,000 tokens, at the provider's list price for the offering, before discounts, credits or committed-use pricing. Tokens are counted by the provider's own tokenizer for that model.

facets.label: Cached input price
facets.definition: The list price of input tokens read from the provider's prompt cache. Cache-write surcharges are a qualifier. `not_offered` when the provider has no prompt cache for this offering, which is a known value, not an unknown one.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: United States dollars per 1,000,000 tokens, at the provider's list price for the offering, before discounts, credits or committed-use pricing. Tokens are counted by the provider's own tokenizer for that model.

facets.label: Batch input price
facets.definition: The list price of input tokens submitted through the provider's asynchronous batch interface. `not_offered` when the provider has no batch interface for this offering.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: United States dollars per 1,000,000 tokens, at the provider's list price for the offering, before discounts, credits or committed-use pricing. Tokens are counted by the provider's own tokenizer for that model.

facets.label: Batch output price
facets.definition: The list price of output tokens returned through the provider's asynchronous batch interface. `not_offered` when the provider has no batch interface for this offering.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: United States dollars per 1,000,000 tokens, at the provider's list price for the offering, before discounts, credits or committed-use pricing. Tokens are counted by the provider's own tokenizer for that model.

facets.label: Cost per task
facets.definition: What one task costs on this offering at list prices, computed per decision from the spec's `task_tokens`: (offering.price.input × input tokens + offering.price.output × output tokens) / 1,000,000. Unknown when either price is unknown. Never authored on a card.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: United States dollars for one task, at list prices: the offering's input price times the spec's input tokens per task, plus its output price times the spec's output tokens per task, divided by 1,000,000. Excludes cached, batch and committed-use pricing.

facets.label: Time to first token
facets.definition: The median time from sending a request to receiving the first output token. Always carries the method: prompt length, output length, effort, region of the client, sample size and date.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: Milliseconds of wall-clock time.

facets.label: Output throughput
facets.definition: The median output throughput of one request after its first token. Always carries the method, as for time to first token. Self-hosted throughput is a labelled estimate only.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: Output tokens generated per second of wall-clock time, measured from the first output token to the last, for a single request.

facets.label: Request rate limit
facets.definition: The documented default request rate limit for a new account at this tier, at the lowest paid usage level the provider documents.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: Requests accepted per 60-second window for one account at the tier the offering names, before any limit increase negotiated by contract.

facets.label: Token rate limit
facets.definition: The documented default token rate limit for a new account at this tier, at the lowest paid usage level the provider documents.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: Tokens (input plus output unless the provider states otherwise, in which case the fact's qualifiers say so) accepted per 60-second window for one account at the tier the offering names.

facets.label: SLA uptime
facets.definition: The monthly uptime the provider commits to in a published service level agreement for this offering, with service credits. A status-page history is not an SLA.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: A percentage from 0 to 100.

facets.label: Data retention
facets.definition: The longest period the provider's terms say it keeps prompts and outputs for this offering by default, for any purpose including abuse monitoring. 0 means not stored after the response. `unbounded` when the terms set no limit.
facets.subject: offering
facets.unit_definition: Calendar days.

facets.label: Trains on customer data
facets.definition: True when the provider's default terms for this offering let it use customer prompts or outputs to train or improve models. An opt-out the customer must take still makes this true.
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: Zero retention available
facets.definition: True when the provider documents that a customer can have prompts and outputs for this offering not stored at all, including for abuse monitoring, whether by default or on request.
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: SOC 2 report
facets.definition: The SOC 2 report type the provider documents for the service this offering runs on, when that report's scope covers the service. `none` when the provider documents no such report. Documented, never "compliant".
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: HIPAA BAA
facets.definition: True when the provider documents that it will sign a HIPAA business associate agreement that covers this offering. Says nothing about whether a customer's use is compliant.
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: FedRAMP level
facets.definition: The FedRAMP authorization level of the cloud service offering this offering runs in, as the FedRAMP marketplace lists it for this model. `none` when not listed.
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: ISO/IEC 27001
facets.definition: True when the provider documents an ISO/IEC 27001 certificate whose scope covers the service this offering runs on.
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: Fine-tuning service
facets.definition: True when the provider sells fine-tuning of this model as a service and serves the tuned model under this offering's terms.
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: Private deployment
facets.definition: True when the provider sells dedicated capacity for this model that is not shared with other customers (provisioned throughput, a dedicated endpoint or deployment in the customer's own cloud account).
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: Harness compatibility
facets.definition: The registered harnesses whose own documentation names this provider as a supported backend for this model. Absence means undocumented.
facets.subject: offering

facets.label: Estimated weight memory
facets.definition: Resident weight memory from verified total parameters at the highest-quality quantisation fitting the named device after the 25% working allowance. One estimate per explicitly named device. A scalar condition or objective requires exactly one device in estate.devices. Never measured or stored.
facets.subject: model
facets.unit_definition: Decimal gigabytes of memory, 1,000,000,000 bytes per GB.

facets.label: Estimated decode speed
facets.definition: Bandwidth roofline from verified active parameters at the memory estimate's quantisation, with 70% efficiency and wide 35% to 85% scenario bounds. Unknown without active parameters, sourced bandwidth or a fitting quantisation. A scalar condition or objective requires exactly one device in estate.devices. Never measured.
facets.subject: model
facets.unit_definition: Output tokens generated per second of wall-clock time, measured from the first output token to the last, for a single request.

refinements.name: Python
refinements.definition: Measures Python software engineering work rather than software engineering as a whole.

templates.name: Coding, best available
templates.tradeoff: Strongest coding evidence, cost no object.
templates.purpose: Find the active coding model with the strongest software-engineering evidence, whatever it costs.

where.reason: Coding work needs a model that generates text and code.
An active model is still supported by its lab or provider.

software_engineering.reason: Rank only by the software-engineering capability estimate.

templates.teaches: With no cost term, the ranking is capability alone; the canvas still shows what each candidate costs.

templates.name: Coding, balanced
templates.tradeoff: Coding strength first, cost as a real second term.
templates.purpose: Find an active coding model with room for a repository that balances coding strength against task cost.

where.reason: Coding work needs a model that generates text and code.
An active model is still supported by its lab or provider.
A large repository needs room for code, tests, and instructions.

software_engineering.reason: Prefer stronger evidence on real software-engineering tasks.

-offering.cost_per_task.reason: Among strong coders, prefer the cheaper task.

templates.teaches: A 70/30 blend keeps capability in charge while letting a large price gap decide close calls.

templates.name: Coding agent on a budget
